segments.text: This New Year's Eve, you might not be able to order food or groceries online because delivery gig workers across India are calling for a nationwide
strike on December 31st. Delivery partners from platforms like Swiggy,
Zumato, Blinket, Zeppto, Amazon, and Flipkart say they've been pushed to a breaking point. Here's what's actually
happening. The protest is being called jointly by the Indian Federation of App-based Transport Workers and the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers Union. Their demands are simple.
Transparent pay, an end to arbitrary ID blocking, mandatory rest breaks, and an immediate roll back of unsafe 10-minute
delivery models. Many workers say they're being forced to take risks on crowded roads, often as the sole breadwinners for their families just to
meet impossible speed targets. This issue has even reached Parliament, where Raav Chada questioned whether ultraast deliveries should exist at all. What do
you think about this issue? Let me know in the comments.
